newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Secret Australia defence review urges expanded role.
newsitem.headline: Secret Australia defence review urges expanded role.

text.p: A secret review of Australia's defence forces has recommended they adopt a more assertive regional role and boost air power and offshore combat ability, a newspaper reported on Saturday.
The Weekend Australian said the review urged increased ability to fight threats beyond Indonesia, which lies only a few hundred kilometres north.

The review called for a dramatic boost in air power, including buying tanker planes for mid-air refueling of the air force's F-111 strike bombers and F/A-18 fighters and new missiles for both, the paper said, citing only "senior sources".
Defence Minister Ian McLachlan would receive the review within two months and make recommendations to the cabinet later this year, the paper said.

Although it called for an increased ability to fight offshore, the review acknowledged that any operations beyond Australia's immediate north would occur only in unusual circumstances and in concert with other nations.
Defence officials were not immediately available for comment.

Australia's year-old conservative government, strapped for cash while watching booming regional powers spend big on defence, two weeks ago announced a plan to slash administrative expenses in the armed forces and boost combat strength.

The Liberal-National government has also shielded the A$10 billion (US$7.75 billion) in annual defence spending from government spending cuts aimed at balancing the budget. All savings will be redirected to new weapons and equipment.
Soon after taking office, McLachlan said he would boost combat capability, including the military's capacity to fight overseas.
Australia and the United States forged a new defence pact last July to boost their joint combat capabilities in the event of regional conflicts.

Although Australia's military is stronger than that of any of its Southeast Asian neighbors, its edge has faded as Asian countries enriched years of runaway economic growth have increased defense spending.
